subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in headless browser for reliable web access without external dependencies

question: Should OpenClaw add browser-backed rendered web access to the managed web_fetch/web_search path, and what owner boundary and security defaults should it use?
rationale: Current code has the pieces for web_fetch, web_search, and a separate browser plugin, but combining them changes product behavior, dependency/runtime packaging, session handling, proxy routing, and arbitrary-web-content security boundaries.

options.title: Keep canonical design tracker
options.body: Use this issue to decide the browser-backed web-access contract and split implementation into reviewed runtime, extraction, session/proxy, and security follow-ups.

options.title: Limit to plugin/API extension
options.body: Keep core web_fetch/web_search unchanged and add only the plugin or SDK seams needed for a ClawHub/browser-provider implementation.

options.title: Decline built-in browser fetch
options.body: Document the existing browser, Browserless/CDP, and provider extraction paths as the supported answer and close the broader built-in request.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical design tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to decide the browser-backed web-access contract and split implementation into reviewed runtime, extraction, session/proxy, and security follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent history shows broad browser, web_fetch, web_search, and security-boundary work across the affected surfaces.
